# cem

```go
import "generator/cem"
```

Package cem contains the Go types for the [Custom Element Manifest](<https://custom-elements-manifest.open-wc.org/>) schema.

### Overview

The schema itself can be found in the [custom element manifest repository](<https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest>).

This package uses a local copy of the schema, downloaded from the [raw file](<https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest/blob/main/schema.json>) in Github.

### Generation of types from the schema

Once the latest JSON version of the CEM schema is downloaded, it is processed by [github.com/atombender/go\\\-jsonschema](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/atombender/go-jsonschema/>) to generate the Go types that can be found in this package.

```
go tool go-jsonschema -o cem.go --only-models -p generator schema.json
```

<a name="CustomElementDeclaration"></a>
## type [CustomElementDeclaration](<https://github.com/bruceesmith/m3e/blob/main/generator/cem/cem.go#L306-L379>)

A description of a custom element class.

Custom elements are JavaScript classes, so this extends from \`ClassDeclaration\` and adds custom\-element\-specific features like attributes, events, and slots.

Note that \`tagName\` in this interface is optional. Tag names are not neccessarily part of a custom element class, but belong to the definition \(often called the "registration"\) or the \`customElements.define\(\)\` call.

Because classes and tag names can only be registered once, there's a one\-to\-one relationship between classes and tag names. For ease of use, we allow the tag name here.

Some packages define and register custom elements in separate modules. In these cases one \`Module\` should contain the \`CustomElement\` without a tagName, and another \`Module\` should contain the \`CustomElementExport\`.

```go

    // The attributes that this element is known to understand.
    Attributes []Attribute `json:"attributes,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"attributes,omitempty" mapstructure:"attributes,omitempty"`

    // CssParts corresponds to the JSON schema field "cssParts".
    CssParts []CssPart `json:"cssParts,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"cssParts,omitempty" mapstructure:"cssParts,omitempty"`

    // CssProperties corresponds to the JSON schema field "cssProperties".
    CssProperties []CssCustomProperty `json:"cssProperties,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"cssProperties,omitempty" mapstructure:"cssProperties,omitempty"`

    // CssStates corresponds to the JSON schema field "cssStates".
    CssStates []CssCustomState `json:"cssStates,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"cssStates,omitempty" mapstructure:"cssStates,omitempty"`

    // Distinguishes a regular JavaScript class from a
    // custom element class
    CustomElement CustomElementDeclarationCustomElement `json:"customElement" yaml:"customElement" mapstructure:"customElement"`

    // Demos corresponds to the JSON schema field "demos".
    Demos []Demo `json:"demos,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"demos,omitempty" mapstructure:"demos,omitempty"`

    // Whether the class or mixin is deprecated.
    // If the value is a string, it's the reason for the deprecation.
    Deprecated interface{} `json:"deprecated,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"deprecated,omitempty" mapstructure:"deprecated,omitempty"`

    // A markdown description of the class.
    Description *string `json:"description,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"description,omitempty" mapstructure:"description,omitempty"`

    // The events that this element fires.
    Events []Event `json:"events,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"events,omitempty" mapstructure:"events,omitempty"`

    // Kind corresponds to the JSON schema field "kind".
    Kind CustomElementDeclarationKind `json:"kind" yaml:"kind" mapstructure:"kind"`

    // Members corresponds to the JSON schema field "members".
    Members []CustomElementDeclarationMembersElem `json:"members,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"members,omitempty" mapstructure:"members,omitempty"`

    // Any class mixins applied in the extends clause of this class.
    //
    // If mixins are applied in the class definition, then the true superclass
    // of this class is the result of applying mixins in order to the superclass.
    //
    // Mixins must be listed in order of their application to the superclass or
    // previous mixin application. This means that the innermost mixin is listed
    // first. This may read backwards from the common order in JavaScript, but
    // matches the order of language used to describe mixin application, like
    // "S with A, B".
    Mixins []Reference `json:"mixins,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"mixins,omitempty" mapstructure:"mixins,omitempty"`

    Slots []Slot `json:"slots,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"slots,omitempty" mapstructure:"slots,omitempty"`

    // Source corresponds to the JSON schema field "source".
    Source *SourceReference `json:"source,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"source,omitempty" mapstructure:"source,omitempty"`

    // A markdown summary suitable for display in a listing.
    Summary *string `json:"summary,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"summary,omitempty" mapstructure:"summary,omitempty"`

    // The superclass of this class.
    //
    // If this class is defined with mixin applications, the prototype chain
    // includes the mixin applications and the true superclass is computed
    // from them.
    Superclass *Reference `json:"superclass,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"superclass,omitempty" mapstructure:"superclass,omitempty"`
```

<a name="JavaScriptModuleDeclarationsElem"></a>
## type [JavaScriptModuleDeclarationsElem](<https://github.com/bruceesmith/m3e/blob/main/generator/cem/cem.go#L762-L850>)

A description of a class mixin.

Mixins are functions which generate a new subclass of a given superclass. This interfaces describes the class and custom element features that are added by the mixin. As such, it extends the CustomElement interface and ClassLike interface.

Since mixins are functions, it also extends the FunctionLike interface. This means a mixin is callable, and has parameters and a return type.

The return type is often hard or impossible to accurately describe in type systems like TypeScript. It requires generics and an \`extends\` operator that TypeScript lacks. Therefore it's recommended that the return type is left empty. The most common form of a mixin function takes a single argument, so consumers of this interface should assume that the return type is the single argument subclassed by this declaration.

A mixin should not have a superclass. If a mixins composes other mixins, they should be listed in the \`mixins\` field.

See \[this article\]\{@link https://justinfagnani.com/2015/12/21/real-mixins-with-javascript-classes/\} for more information on the classmixin pattern in JavaScript.

<a name="MixinDeclaration"></a>
## type [MixinDeclaration](<https://github.com/bruceesmith/m3e/blob/main/generator/cem/cem.go#L911-L958>)

A description of a class mixin.

Mixins are functions which generate a new subclass of a given superclass. This interfaces describes the class and custom element features that are added by the mixin. As such, it extends the CustomElement interface and ClassLike interface.

Since mixins are functions, it also extends the FunctionLike interface. This means a mixin is callable, and has parameters and a return type.

The return type is often hard or impossible to accurately describe in type systems like TypeScript. It requires generics and an \`extends\` operator that TypeScript lacks. Therefore it's recommended that the return type is left empty. The most common form of a mixin function takes a single argument, so consumers of this interface should assume that the return type is the single argument subclassed by this declaration.

A mixin should not have a superclass. If a mixins composes other mixins, they should be listed in the \`mixins\` field.

See \[this article\]\{@link https://justinfagnani.com/2015/12/21/real-mixins-with-javascript-classes/\} for more information on the classmixin pattern in JavaScript.

```go
type MixinDeclaration struct {
    // Whether the class or mixin is deprecated.
    // If the value is a string, it's the reason for the deprecation.
    Deprecated interface{} `json:"deprecated,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"deprecated,omitempty" mapstructure:"deprecated,omitempty"`

    // A markdown description of the class.
    Description *string `json:"description,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"description,omitempty" mapstructure:"description,omitempty"`

    // Kind corresponds to the JSON schema field "kind".
    Kind MixinDeclarationKind `json:"kind" yaml:"kind" mapstructure:"kind"`

    // Members corresponds to the JSON schema field "members".
    Members []MixinDeclarationMembersElem `json:"members,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"members,omitempty" mapstructure:"members,omitempty"`

    // Any class mixins applied in the extends clause of this class.
    //
    // If mixins are applied in the class definition, then the true superclass
    // of this class is the result of applying mixins in order to the superclass.
    //
    // Mixins must be listed in order of their application to the superclass or
    // previous mixin application. This means that the innermost mixin is listed
    // first. This may read backwards from the common order in JavaScript, but
    // matches the order of language used to describe mixin application, like
    // "S with A, B".
    Mixins []Reference `json:"mixins,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"mixins,omitempty" mapstructure:"mixins,omitempty"`

    // Name corresponds to the JSON schema field "name".
    Name string `json:"name" yaml:"name" mapstructure:"name"`

    // Parameters corresponds to the JSON schema field "parameters".
    Parameters []Parameter `json:"parameters,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"parameters,omitempty" mapstructure:"parameters,omitempty"`

    // Return corresponds to the JSON schema field "return".
    Return *MixinDeclarationReturn `json:"return,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"return,omitempty" mapstructure:"return,omitempty"`

    // Source corresponds to the JSON schema field "source".
    Source *SourceReference `json:"source,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"source,omitempty" mapstructure:"source,omitempty"`

    // A markdown summary suitable for display in a listing.
    Summary *string `json:"summary,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"summary,omitempty" mapstructure:"summary,omitempty"`

    // The superclass of this class.
    //
    // If this class is defined with mixin applications, the prototype chain
    // includes the mixin applications and the true superclass is computed
    // from them.
    Superclass *Reference `json:"superclass,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"superclass,omitempty" mapstructure:"superclass,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="Reference"></a>
## type [Reference](<https://github.com/bruceesmith/m3e/blob/main/generator/cem/cem.go#L1069-L1078>)

A reference to an export of a module.

All references are required to be publically accessible, so the canonical representation of a reference is the export it's available from.

\`package\` should generally refer to an npm package name. If \`package\` is undefined then the reference is local to this package. If \`module\` is undefined the reference is local to the containing module.

References to global symbols like \`Array\`, \`HTMLElement\`, or \`Event\` should use a \`package\` name of \`"global:"\`.

```go

    // Module corresponds to the JSON schema field "module".
    Module *string `json:"module,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"module,omitempty" mapstructure:"module,omitempty"`

    // Name corresponds to the JSON schema field "name".
    Name string `json:"name" yaml:"name" mapstructure:"name"`

    // Package corresponds to the JSON schema field "package".
    Package *string `json:"package,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"package,omitempty" mapstructure:"package,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="SchemaJson"></a>
## type [SchemaJson](<https://github.com/bruceesmith/m3e/blob/main/generator/cem/cem.go#L1091-L1108>)

The top\-level interface of a custom elements manifest file.

Because custom elements are JavaScript classes, describing a custom element may require describing arbitrary JavaScript concepts like modules, classes, functions, etc. So custom elements manifests are capable of documenting the elements in a package, as well as those JavaScript concepts.

The modules described in a package should be the public entrypoints that other packages may import from. Multiple modules may export the same object via re\-exports, but in most cases a package should document the single canonical export that should be used.

```go
type SchemaJson struct {
    // Whether the package is deprecated.
    // If the value is a string, it's the reason for the deprecation.
    Deprecated interface{} `json:"deprecated,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"deprecated,omitempty" mapstructure:"deprecated,omitempty"`

    // An array of the modules this package contains.
    Modules []JavaScriptModule `json:"modules" yaml:"modules" mapstructure:"modules"`

    // The Markdown to use for the main readme of this package.
    //
    // This can be used to override the readme used by Github or npm if that
    // file contains information irrelevant to custom element catalogs and
    // documentation viewers.
    Readme *string `json:"readme,omitempty,omitzero" yaml:"readme,omitempty" mapstructure:"readme,omitempty"`

    // The version of the schema used in this file.
    SchemaVersion string `json:"schemaVersion" yaml:"schemaVersion" mapstructure:"schemaVersion"`
}
```
